- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates; adjust downward by 5–10% to avoid missing upside reversal.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above recent high); cap forecast at 1.5x recent high for 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to continue falling; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period rallies; add 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment in final 5–7 days if sentiment turns positive.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., negative → positive → negative), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for momentum shifts.
